correctness.rationale: For the precise background-limited objective, S'=N/(2T^(3/2)) with N=2TI−E. This N satisfies N(0)=0, is positive near zero, and tends to −a/λ−b/μ. Differentiation gives N'=a(1−2λT)e^(−λT)+b(1−2μT)e^(−μT). Multiplying by e^(λT) and differentiating twice leaves b d e^(−dT)(d+4μ−2μdT) with d=μ−λ>0, so Rolle bounds the distinct positive zeros of N' by three. The zero of N at zero then bounds its distinct positive zeros by three as well. Three strict maxima would force at least five critical points including the two interior minima, even when some critical points are degenerate. This is the decisive bound; four alternating sampled signs, as opposed to four sign changes, require only three intervening extrema, so the informal sentence at line 36 is unnecessary. An independent exact Fraction enclosure, using degrees 12 and 13 at x/32 before powering, bounds 10⁶ N at 1/20,1/8,1/3,1 in (28439,28440), (−30229,−30228), (27711,27712), (−63029,−63028). Three disjoint sign crossings exhaust the allowed zeros, giving strict max/min/max. Widths for the reported degree-16/17 method check separately. For one mode, N' changes from positive to negative exactly once while N starts at 0 and has a negative limit, proving the unique strict maximum.
